solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Signal to setter, to follow when crossing road

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: one piece crossing another lies across it, so the road sits inside the word for 'when'

parts.note: while means at the time that, as when does
ST, short for street, stands in for road

explanation.surface: Advice to someone, perhaps a dog walker, about what to do while crossing a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the dog breed; 'crossing' signals one piece lying inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-pitched whistle is used to call or command a dog, such as a setter.

clue.text: Heartlessly trick old Venetian

indicators.note: without its heart, so the central letter of the word for trick is dropped

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: A cruel deception practised on an elderly man from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes the middle D of DODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected chief magistrate who ruled the Venetian republic for centuries.

clue.text: Seriously rough sheds start to lean

indicators.note: sheds means casts off, so a letter is removed from the word for rough

parts.note: a gravelly voice or surface is rough and harsh

indicators.note: the start of the word lean is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Rough sheds that are beginning to lean are a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds' drops one L (the start of 'lean') from GRAVELLY. 'Seriously' looks like an adverb on the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs describing something done in a solemn, grave manner.

clue.text: Exceptionally, Mr G E Meredith means to cut the privet?

indicators.note: done exceptionally means done in an unusual way, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called G E Meredith, unusually, has the job of cutting the privet hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' signals an anagram of MRGEMEREDITH. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is a common hedging shrub, and a powered trimming tool is the means of cutting it.

clue.text: Butcher's fine cuts secure introduction to Ike

indicators.note: one piece cutting another goes into it, so fine is set inside the word for secure

parts.note: to shut a door is to secure it
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A butcher's fine cuts of meat win over a man named Ike.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTCHER'S is rhyming slang: 'butcher's hook' = look. 'cuts' puts F inside SHUT, then I from Ike follows. 'Butcher's' seems to be a meat shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a quick look: a butcher's (hook) and a shufti, from Arabic.

clue.text: Endless coffee, chilled, with decorative pattern

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the coffee is dropped

parts.note: a latte is a milky espresso coffee
iced means made cold, chilled

explanation.surface: An endless supply of iced coffee, served with a decorative pattern in the foam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last E from LATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross openwork design, so a latticed object bears that decorative pattern.

clue.text: Crazy Ottoman leaving large island for cliff

indicators.note: these pieces leave, that is depart from, the island's name, so they are removed from it

parts.note: Madagascar is a large island off south-east Africa
mad means crazy
an aga was a military commander in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A deranged Turk abandons a big island and heads for a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes MAD and AGA off the front of MADAGASCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky outcrop or cliff face, common in northern English place names.

clue.text: Bob is brusque and revolting, I agree

parts.note: curt means brusque, abrupt in manner

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the words for agreement are read backwards

parts.note: yes is how one says I agree

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is abrupt and disgusting, and the speaker concurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns YES into SEY. 'Bob' is not a name but a verb: to bob is to make a quick curtsey.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a brief bending of the knees as a mark of respect, a quick curtsey.

clue.text: Perhaps ODIs totally enthralling Gershwin?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the run of words holds the solution within it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one-day international cricket matches totally captivated the composer Gershwin.
explanation.walkthrough: ODIs are one-day internationals in cricket. 'enthralling' signals letters held inside the clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue, so he is an example of a composer of rhapsodies; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Germaine regularly intimidates relatives

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one, starting from the first

parts.note: daunts means intimidates or discourages

explanation.surface: A woman named Germaine routinely frightens her family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of Germaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Great-aunts, the sisters of one's grandparents, are family members.

clue.text: What's found in school in West Coast states

parts.note: OR is the postal code of Oregon, a state on the US West Coast
CA is the postal code of California, the other West Coast state the plural points to

explanation.surface: A question about the subjects taught in schools in the western United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Coast states' together names two Pacific states, Oregon and California, by their postal codes. 'school' suggests pupils, but it is the collective noun for a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer whales travel in groups, and a school is a collective name for such sea creatures.

clue.text: Equable pair mentioned in Genesis kneel awkwardly

parts.note: Onan and Eve are two people who appear in the Book of Genesis

indicators.note: done awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters of kneel are jumbled

explanation.surface: A calm couple from the Bible go down on their knees clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges KNEEL as NKEEL. 'pair' looks like a couple (Adam and Eve), but it is two separate Genesis figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a steady, untroubled state, as a ship kept level, which is what an equable temperament is.

clue.text: Pianist sees red when playing and bans traffic from street

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters at play, moving freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist gets angry during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges PIANISTSEESRED. 'playing' looks like the pianist's own activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedestrianise a road is to close it to vehicles so only people on foot may use it.

clue.text: Cook dropping round coeliac menu to further Christian unity

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so these letters are rearranged
dropping means leaving out, so one letter is lost from the pool

parts.note: a round shape is a ring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A chef abandons a circular menu for people with coeliac disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' and 'dropping' mean the letters of COELIAC MENU, less an O, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecumenical movement aims to promote cooperation and unity among the different Christian churches.

clue.text: Constant publicity about Dior's last perfume

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: about means around, so the publicity goes around the next piece

parts.note: hype is exaggerated publicity

indicators.note: last here asks for the final letter of the designer's name

explanation.surface: Endless promotion surrounding the latest scent from the House of Dior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside HYPE after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chypre is a family of fragrances built on citrus, oakmoss and labdanum, named after Cyprus.

clue.text: Perceptive of you to have lamented housing

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: keened means wailed in mourning, lamented
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Praising someone as sharp for having mourned the loss of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like accommodation in the surface but signals one word held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp-sighted notices details quickly, so they are perceptive.

clue.text: Gully containing source of water for expedition

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the gully wraps around the water source

parts.note: a ditch is a narrow channel like a gully
a spa is a mineral spring, a source of water

explanation.surface: A ravine holding a spring is the goal of an exploring party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but here it means speed, promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean speed and efficiency in getting something done, as in acting with dispatch.

clue.text: Millions type, millions help; this female works in dairy

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
ilk means type or kind
M again, for million
aid means help

explanation.surface: Millions of a certain kind and millions in assistance support a dairy worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional term for a young woman who draws milk from cows in a dairy.

clue.text: Laughing out loud over fat idler

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it, so first

parts.note: LOL is internet shorthand for laughing out loud
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Someone laughs out loud at a fat layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat idler' reads as one phrase, but 'fat' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollard is an old word for an idle loafer, one who lolls about; also the name of a medieval religious group.

clue.text: They happen to make smooth talkers "discontented"

parts.note: to even a surface is to make it smooth

indicators.note: without contents, so only the outside letters of talkers are kept

explanation.surface: Things occur that turn slick speakers unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' means emptied: TALKERS loses its middle, leaving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are occurrences, things that take place.

clue.text: Duck heard on lake intercepting two army swimmers

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, nought or naught

indicators.note: intercepting means cutting in between, so lake goes between the two numerals

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck can be heard on a lake, caught between two military units of swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' means having arms: these cephalopods have many tentacles. A duck in cricket is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautili are sea-dwelling cephalopods with many arms or tentacles, so they are swimmers equipped with arms.

clue.text: Conservative way to reverse decay

indicators.note: reverse means read the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: The Conservative way of turning back decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns TORYRD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that destroys timber in buildings.

clue.text: Splendid manure ruined? Don't despair!

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's fine compost has been spoiled, but someone urges them not to lose hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges SPLENDIDMANURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means 'never despairing', an urging not to lose hope.

clue.text: Leer at yogi and flee, unclothed

indicators.note: with clothing taken off, so each word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Stare lewdly at a yoga practitioner and run away naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclothed' strips the outside letters of 'yogi' and 'flee'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone lecherously, which is what leering does.

clue.text: Blackguard besieging hot country

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the rogue goes around the letter for hot

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a blackguard
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A villain lays siege to a sweltering nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besieging' puts H inside CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Undernourished chap, very embarrassed at first, tucked into bird

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the initials go inside the bird

parts.note: a starling is a common songbird

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A thin man, deeply ashamed at first, tucks into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating, but it signals insertion of V and E into STARLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A starveling is a person who is thin and underfed.

clue.text: Swimming pool image back to front

indicators.note: back to front means its last letter comes round to the front

parts.note: an idol is an image worshipped as a god

explanation.surface: A picture of an outdoor pool shown the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final L of IDOL to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Talk with woman, mistress of big house

parts.note: chat means talk
Elaine is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A conversation with a woman who runs a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the female head of a large household, holding its keys.
